clue.text: Saving 60 minutes one fellow races round

indicators.note: the races go round, enclosing the words that come before them

parts.note: first half of TT, the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A thrifty man saves an hour by racing around.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races; the two Ts wrap round HR, I and F.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful economy with money, the habit of putting money by.

clue.text: Irritating drunk tries to ring me

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the next word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An annoying drunk keeps trying to phone me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call or a container signal, but here it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means tedious and annoying, which is what irritating means.

clue.text: Coach dashed round for list of runners

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for dashed goes round the coach

parts.note: a railway coach is a car

explanation.surface: A coach hurries round to pick up a team list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list of runners' suggests athletes, but the runners are horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecard is the printed programme listing the horses running at a race meeting.

parts.note: surface reading: unable to tolerate something any longer
cryptic reading: literally no room left in the stomach after eating

explanation.walkthrough: 'stomach' means put up with in the surface, but the answer takes it literally as having eaten enough.
explanation.definitionFit: After a big meal you have no room to eat more, the literal state of being sated.

indicators.note: acting mysteriously suggests the letters are behaving in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A wonderful man lets out a mysterious sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is informal British praise meaning excellent or terrific.

clue.text: Awfully dim male actor is sensational!

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters are put together in a poor order and must be fixed

explanation.surface: A not-very-bright actor gives a terrible, over-the-top performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Melodramatic behaviour is exaggerated and showy, aimed at causing a stir, as sensational suggests.

indicators.note: being on a ship means being aboard it, so the article goes inside the vessel

parts.note: board stands for a steamship, SS, as in going on board
IT is an article: a thing

explanation.surface: Someone sets a newspaper article on a board.
explanation.walkthrough: On board is a crossword convention: put inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit someone or something is to set it down in position, so it places it.

clue.text: Trade is bound by standards of perfection

indicators.note: something bound by another is tied up inside it, so trade sits within the word is

explanation.surface: Commerce is held to high ethical standards.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' in 'is bound by' doubles as letters and part of the indicator phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are the perfect standards a person aims for, principles of excellence.

explanation.surface: A late-night encounter with a woman called Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is a crossword convention for the middle letter of night, not twelve o'clock; Elizabeth is the Queen's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is used to mean whether one is male or female, as sex does.

clue.text: Recollect man leaving here by request

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bring back to mind
second meaning: summoning someone home, as a government does with an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a man who left on being asked to.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: an envoy who leaves his post because he has been asked back has had this done to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means remember, and also an official order summoning a person back home.

parts.note: a slat is a thin strip of wood

indicators.note: vocal means spoken, so the next word is taken by sound

parts.note: the seabird sounds like this word

explanation.surface: A woman of poor repute does a striptease and a singing turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slut's' reads as Slut is: the definition then the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A slattern is a dirty, untidy woman, a dated insult equivalent to slut.

clue.text: Compliment cult on a great broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone praises a cult following for a great programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To congratulate someone is to praise them on an achievement, which is to compliment them.

clue.text: When cold ask cook about fire

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the rearranged word surrounds the cold letter
to cook something is to doctor or rework it, so the next word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An instruction to ask the cook to light a fire when it gets cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire and to sack both mean to dismiss someone from their job.

clue.text: Sullen doctor loves embracing youth leader

indicators.note: a leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of youth is wanted
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the doctor's letters wrap round the loves

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O; two of them

explanation.surface: A sulky doctor dotes on a young man in his care.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is zero in tennis scoring, so it is the letter O, here twice; a leader is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moody describes someone sulky and bad-tempered, which is what sullen means.

parts.note: cryptic reading: royal and navy are both shades of one colour

explanation.walkthrough: Royal Navy reads as the fleet, but each word is a shade: royal blue and navy blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal and navy are both named varieties of this colour, so either is an example of it.

clue.text: Foolhardy trainee is reversing' empty lorry

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word is reads the other way

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plates

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of lorry

explanation.surface: A learner driver recklessly reverses an empty lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The order in the answer is the reversed word, then the trainee, then the shell of lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly can mean rash and lacking sense, close to reckless or foolhardy.

explanation.surface: A page at the back carries a picture in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a full-page printed picture in a book, often on glossy paper.

indicators.note: swinging means moving to and fro, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman named Maria swings a bare leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile originally means of an age and suitability to wed, a dictionary synonym for this word.

clue.text: People after teams of church workers

parts.note: teams in a match are sides

explanation.surface: People chase after teams of church volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the people behind the teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidesmen are assistants to churchwardens in the Church of England, who hand out books and take collections.

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the journalist goes round the wife

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer gets married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes a wife' reads as marrying, which hints at the answer's other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and support it.

clue.text: Collapsing as panel attempts to make jokes

indicators.note: something collapsing falls apart, so the next words' letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A panel show's efforts at humour fall flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantries are light, polite remarks or small jests made in conversation.

indicators.note: when inside means the following letters are set inside the taxi

parts.note: leaning on a wall is leaning against it

explanation.surface: A conversation in a taxi gets loud and argumentative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' tempts CON, which leaves too many Cs; it is ON. F is forte, loud in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Confab is short for confabulation, an informal talk or chat.

indicators.note: things swimming move about freely, so the letters of the next word drift into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is stiff after a swim across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal manners are stiff and ceremonious rather than relaxed.

clue.text: Musician's order is to include duck

definitions.note: the musician's instrument: the possessive stands for the thing he plays

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the order goes round the duck

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket

explanation.surface: A musician has been instructed to add a duck to his act.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour; a duck is a zero in cricket, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodwind instrument is what an orchestral player in that section owns and plays.

clue.text: I go round this Italian city

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the word for go wraps the letter I

explanation.surface: A tourist describes travelling around an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: TURN is split around I: TUR-I-N.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the capital of Piedmont in northern Italy, home of Fiat and Juventus.

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the turned word goes round the queen
returning means going back, so the word on is read backwards

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor hugs a returning queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the Roman emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned.

indicators.note: making something better means altering it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer is said to be a great deal better.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with the voice range between soprano and tenor.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone rolls something up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a roll or list of people who take turns at duties.

indicators.note: the letters of the word are taken apart and reused rather than the word itself

explanation.surface: A well-known woman receives letters by airmail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' looks like post, which fits airmail, but it asks for the letters of airmail rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something familiar is commonly known or recognised, a plain synonym.

parts.note: a cos is a long-leaved lettuce

explanation.surface: A doctor is chasing a lettuce plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the doctor's piece behind the lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmos is a garden flower of the daisy family, grown for its bright blooms.

explanation.surface: People recall having yelled 'ring round' to one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like an instruction to go round something, but it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to shout loudly in a deep voice, like a bull.

indicators.note: to seize is to grab and hold, so the man's name holds the girl's

explanation.surface: A sunburnt man grabs hold of a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin that has been browned by sunlight is tanned, a near synonym of sunburnt.
